records.title: Viscosity variation in fluid flows across scales
records.directory_context: Viscosity variation in fluid flows across scales Arjun Sharma, Ritabrata Thakur, Sharath Jose, and Rama Govindarajan Rev. Mod. Phys. 98 , 045002 (2026) - Published 26 October, 2026 Although most treatments of fluid mechanics consider the fluid viscosity to be constant or uniform, many systems have a viscosity that varies in time or space. Examples arise in microbial habitats, in the ocean, and in Earth’s mantle. In this review, the authors explain how viscosity gradients occur in real systems, examine how these gradients lead to new phenomena at both low and high Reynolds number, and highlight open research questions.
